GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Daerah is Bengkalis Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Bengkalis Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Bengkalis. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus of Bengkalis Regency as an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional People's Representative Council in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties, either temporarily or based on a court order. 6. 7. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. Child protection is all activities to guarantee

8. and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against the physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action

10. based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship for women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. Threat of violence is any act unlawfully in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of

12. means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or hardship

13. physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 14. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father

16. and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 17. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 19, Non-Governmental Organization hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or

20. indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Bengkalis Regency area. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and society in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. Assistance is an effort made by a person or

25. representative from an institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to

26. victims in accordance with established standards. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to

27. physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person

28. who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against

30. women and children that is gender responsive. 31. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bengkalis Regency.

Article 12

Other violence as referred to in Article letter constitutes threats of violence and coercion.

1. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause (2) fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where_ a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will (3).

Article 26

Forms of services to victims as referred to in (1 in Article 24 letter b, are as follows:

a. services to women and children victims of acts of violence, include:

1. complaint, consultation and counseling services;
2. accompaniment services;
3. health services;
4. legal aid services;
5. repatriation and social reintegration services; and
6. social rehabilitation services.

b. in addition to the forms of services regulated in letter a, special services are also provided which include:

1. pick-up services; and/or
2. medical and psychological referral services.

Forms of services as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a and letter b, shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus (2) in accordance with minimum service standards established by the government.

Further provisions regarding the implementation of services (3) as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

1. The community has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in handling victims of acts of violence.

Article 19

Parents, guardians and/or family legally have (1) full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims. Parents and/or family must carry out prevention (2) of all forms of violence by providing guidance and example in accordance with religious teachings and prevailing norms. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to certain reasons cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then (3) the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Paragraph Community

CHAPTER VII CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 45

Any person who intentionally commits violence against women and children as referred to in Article up to Article 12 shall be subject to criminal sanctions as regulated in laws and regulations.

Paragraph General

Article 22

The Regional Government, in implementing the provision of protection of women and children from acts of violence, carries out the following activities:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Paragraph Prevention

Paragraph Regional Government

Article 18

The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government (1) as referred to in Article 17 letter a, include:

a. preparing and implementing programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implementing the protection of women and children;
c. supervising services to victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocating budget for the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity.

In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities (2) as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government prepares programs and activities for the protection of women and children in a regional action plan which is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan. The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government (3) as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their main duties and functions. Further provisions regarding the regional action plan (4) as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be further stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Paragraph Parents, Guardians and/or Family

Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is the Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children in the working area of several Sub-districts at the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bengkalis Regency. 32. 33. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating efforts to prevent and handle trafficking in persons. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against

34. children and women at the Sub-district and Village/Kelurahan level. 35. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material/immaterial benefits. 36. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 37. Empowerment is a process of developing independence and welfare of a person or society by increasing knowledge and skills to meet their living needs both economically and socially. 38. Restorative Justice is the settlement of criminal cases by involving the perpetrator, victim, family of the perpetrator/victim, and other related parties to jointly seek a fair settlement by emphasizing restoration to the original state, and not retaliation. Article

Protection of women and children is carried out based on the principles of: humanity; justice and gender equality; c. protection; d. best interests of women and children; e. non-discrimination; andf. empowerment. Article

This Regional Regulation is intended as:

a. fulfillment of the rights of children and women in the context of protection and prevention of violence for children and women in the Region; andb. guidelines for the Regional Government and society to provide protection, services, medical rehabilitation, social rehabilitation and empowerment for women and children victims of acts of violence. Article

The purpose of protection of women and children in this Regional Regulation is: a. to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; eliminate all forms of violence and exploitation against women and children; protect and provide a sense of security for victims

c. (women and children); provide services to women and children victims

d. acts of violence and carry out rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children victims of acts of violence with the involvement of business actors; improve cooperation and partnerships with

e. the involvement of companies to implement empowerment and protection of women and children from various acts of violence; implement women's empowerment to improve the quality of life of women; andf. establish and implement policies and programs/activities for the fulfillment of children's rights. Article The scope of the implementation of protection of women and children regulated in this Regional Regulation includes: prevention of violence against women and children; a. b. provision of services for women and children victims of violence; institutions; cooperation and partnerships; d. funding; e. investigation; and

f. g. criminal provisions.

Part Two

Implementation of Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence

Article 40

The Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons as referred to in Article 38 letter b, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling (1 trafficking in persons.

The Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children (2) as referred to in Article 38 letter c, is a functional work unit that provides integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women.

Provisions regarding the Task Force for the Prevention and (3) Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons and the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 41

In order to achieve the objectives of the protection of women and children as referred to in Article 4, the Regional Government may cooperate with other parties in accordance with (1) the provisions of laws and regulations.

Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: (2)

a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; andd. provision of evidence and witnesses.

Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (3) (2) is set forth in the form of _Joint Agreement and/or Cooperation Agreement_ in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material/immaterial benefits. 36. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 37. Empowerment is a process of developing independence and welfare of a person or society by increasing knowledge and skills to meet their living needs both economically and socially. 38. Restorative Justice is the settlement of criminal cases by involving the perpetrator, victim, family of the perpetrator/victim, and other related parties to jointly seek a fair settlement by emphasizing restoration to the original state, and not retaliation. Paragraph General

Article 22

The Regional Government, in implementing the provision of protection of women and children from acts of violence, carries out the following activities:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

Paragraph Prevention

Article 19

Parents, guardians and/or family legally have (1) full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims. Parents and/or family must carry out prevention (2) of all forms of violence by providing guidance and example in accordance with religious teachings and prevailing norms. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to certain reasons cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then (3) the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20

1. The community has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in handling victims of acts of violence.
